hypotheses.cause: Service catalog-api targetPort is misconfigured to port 8080 instead of containerPort 8081 (or named port catalog-http), causing Endpoints and kube-proxy/routing to direct service traffic to an unlistening port on ready backend pods.
supports: Service 'catalog-api' in spec.ports specifies port 80 with targetPort 8080.
Endpoints subsets publish port 8080 for pod IPs 10.42.0.35 and 10.42.0.36.
Deployment 'catalog-api' and Pod specs explicitly define containerPort 8081 named 'catalog-http'.
ConfigMap 'catalog-nginx' configures Nginx server listening directive to 'listen 8081;'.
Readiness probes targeting containerPort 'catalog-http' (8081) succeed, marking pods Ready.

hypotheses.cause: Catalog application container workload is misconfigured to listen on port 8081 instead of the intended port 8080 expected by the Service.
contradicts: Deployment spec, Pod spec, and ConfigMap 'catalog-nginx' are all consistently authored for port 8081 / 'catalog-http'.
Readiness probe explicitly tests port 'catalog-http' (8081) and reports Ready status.
supports: Service targetPort is 8080 while pod container listening port is 8081.

hypotheses.cause: Service selector mismatch is attaching the Service to incorrect backend pods or failing to select valid pods.
contradicts: Service selector is 'app.kubernetes.io/name: catalog-api', which matches the Deployment template labels.
Endpoints object successfully resolves and lists the running pod IPs (10.42.0.35, 10.42.0.36).

hypotheses.cause: Catalog API pods are unhealthy, unready, or stuck in crash loops preventing traffic delivery.
contradicts: Deployment status indicates 2/2 ready and available replicas.
Both pod status conditions report Ready=True and ContainersReady=True.
supports: Initial startup warning events recorded readiness probe connection refusal before Nginx initialized.

payload.rationale: Service catalog-api in namespace proofix-case-03 was misconfigured with targetPort 8080, causing Endpoints to direct traffic to an unlistening port on backend pods listening on port 8081. Patching targetPort to 8081 aligns traffic routing with the container listening port.
payload.rollback_trigger: HTTP 5xx rate >= 0.001 or p95 latency >= 200ms across evaluation windows after applying the Service targetPort patch.

success_criteria.description: Service traffic to catalog-api successfully routes to backend pods on port 8081 with HTTP 5xx error rate < 0.001 and p95 latency < 200ms for 3 consecutive windows.

critical_claims.claim: Service catalog-api in namespace proofix-case-03 configured port 80 with targetPort 8080.
The catalog-api Pods and Deployment template define containerPort 8081 (named catalog-http), and ConfigMap catalog-nginx configures Nginx to listen on port 8081.
Endpoints for catalog-api advertised port 8080 for backend pod IPs 10.42.0.35 and 10.42.0.36, routing service traffic to an unlistening port.
Service catalog-api was patched to remediate the targetPort configuration.
Post-remediation SLO evaluations show 0.0 error rate and p95 latency well within the 200ms threshold across consecutive observation windows.

closure.summary: Hypothesis H1 is confirmed: the catalog-api Service in namespace proofix-case-03 had its targetPort misconfigured to 8080 instead of containerPort 8081 (catalog-http) where the Nginx container listens. Patching the Service targetPort resolved the routing failure and satisfied all SLO requirements.
